headline: A PLAN FOR TOTAL WAR
text: In December nineteen forty-nine, American planners drafted a secret strike to destroy an empire, betting on an arsenal that did not yet exist.
docket: WAR PLAN CONCEPTION · DOC REF JCS-1949

headline: 300 ATOMIC BOMBS · 100 CITIES
text: Codenamed Dropshot, it projected war in nineteen fifty-seven: three hundred atomic bombs across one hundred cities, destroying eighty-five percent of Soviet industry.
docket: TARGET LIST & DAMAGE · DOC REF JCS-1949

headline: NO MISSILES · BOMBERS ONLY
text: With no missiles yet invented, every bomb required Strategic Air Command heavy bombers, flying Arctic routes from forward bases.
docket: SAC FLIGHT PROFILES · DOC REF JCS-1949

headline: THE MONOPOLY ENDS · RDS-1
text: In August nineteen forty-nine, Moscow detonated R-D-S-one at Semipalatinsk, ending America's atomic monopoly years ahead of schedule.

headline: WAR PLAN SHELVED
text: Dropshot was never launched. Once both superpowers held the bomb, a first strike meant mutual destruction, creating nuclear deterrence.

headline: THE PAPER ARSENAL
text: Declassified in nineteen seventy-seven, Dropshot held a final irony: in nineteen forty-nine, America had only about one hundred seventy warheads for a three-hundred-bomb war.
